Pivot results into an analysis matrix

as_wide.Rd

Pivots results into one column per item, holding the probability of the target label.

Usage

as_wide(
  results,
  ...,
  target = NULL,
  value = c("prob_renorm", "expected_score"),
  prefix = "",
  dichotomize = FALSE,
  keep = character(0),
  drop_incomplete = TRUE
)

Arguments

results

A fathom_results object from measure() or read_checkpoints().

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

target

A string naming the label whose probability fills each cell. Defaults to the first label for a multi-item instrument, and to NULL for an exclusive instrument or a single question, where every label gets its own column.

value

A string naming the column that supplies the value. Defaults to "prob_renorm", the probability conditioned on the model having answered with one of your labels at all. That is the quantity a human coder given the same categories would have produced, and it is what validate_sample() and the expected score read, so a matrix built here can be compared against either without changing quantity partway through.

"expected_score" requires an instrument built with scores, and returns one column per item rather than one per label, since an expected score is one number per document and item. On an item whose pct_extreme_renorm in item_report() sits near 1 it bunches at the scores themselves, so it ranks documents more reliably than it measures the distances between them.

prefix

A string prepended to column names. Default is "".

dichotomize

A logical value indicating whether to threshold at 0.5 and return integers. Default is FALSE.

keep

A character vector of row-level columns to carry alongside. Each must hold one value per document, since this returns one row per document. A column that varies within a document is refused rather than allowed to widen the pivot. Default is character(0).

drop_incomplete

A logical value indicating whether to drop documents missing any item. Default is TRUE.

Value

A tibble, one row per document, carrying id, then any keep columns, then the pivoted values. Column names take prefix if given.

What the value columns are depends on the arguments, and there are three shapes.

  • Naming target gives one column per item, holding that label's probability. The usual shape for an instrument of independent binary items, and the one a measurement model wants.

  • Leaving target as NULL gives one column per label on a single-item instrument, or one per item and label combination on an instrument of several, named item_label. Use it when every label matters rather than one.

  • value = "expected_score" gives one column per item, since an expected score is already one number per document and item. Requires an instrument built with scores, and cannot be combined with dichotomize.

Values are probabilities, or integers when dichotomize = TRUE. A failed, truncated, or all-absent record becomes NA, and drop_incomplete decides whether its document leaves the frame. Either way the count is reported rather than left to be noticed.

Normalizing across items

There is no argument to normalize across items. K independent binary items do not form a distribution, as each probability comes from its own softmax over its own two-token distribution. Dividing them by their sum produces a number that looks like a proportion and is not one.

An exclusive instrument is the exception. Its K labels share one softmax at one position, so its rows do sum to one and are comparable across categories. This detects that from the results and defaults target to NULL, giving one column per category.

Exclusive results

instrument(..., exclusive = TRUE) produces a real distribution. Row sums are meaningful, minus whatever leaked outside the label set. On an exclusive instrument scored on discovered first tokens, that remainder is mostly the gap left by the approximation, since the probability of a first token is an upper bound on the probability of the label it opens.

See also

measure() for the results it pivots and item_report() for a summary per item.

Examples

# Results from a real run ship with the package, so this needs no server.
p <- system.file("extdata", "vignette_results.rds", package = "fathom")
baked <- readRDS(p)
res <- baked$res_six

# An exclusive instrument gives one column per category.
head(as_wide(res, prefix = "p_"))
#> 
#> Note     Exclusive instrument. Rows are a distribution, sums 1.000 to 1.000.
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   id       p_1      p_2      p_3       p_4           p_5       p_6
#>   <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 uk_001 0     0        6.65e- 6 1.000e+ 0 0.0000000147  3.17 e- 7
#> 2 uk_002 1.000 5.26e-11 0        0         0             1.28 e-10
#> 3 uk_003 0     0        0        4.87 e-10 0.00000000110 1.000e+ 0
#> 4 uk_004 0     5.54e-10 6.46e-10 1.35 e- 7 1.000         1.58 e- 6
#> 5 uk_005 0     6.08e- 8 1.00e- 1 9.00 e- 1 0.00000143    1.98 e- 6
#> 6 uk_006 1.000 0        0        0         0             1.39 e-10
head(as_wide(res, prefix = "p_", dichotomize = TRUE))
#> 
#> Note     Exclusive instrument. Rows are a distribution, sums 1.000 to 1.000.
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   id       p_1   p_2   p_3   p_4   p_5   p_6
#>   <chr>  <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int>
#> 1 uk_001     0     0     0     1     0     0
#> 2 uk_002     1     0     0     0     0     0
#> 3 uk_003     0     0     0     0     0     1
#> 4 uk_004     0     0     0     0     1     0
#> 5 uk_005     0     0     0     1     0     0
#> 6 uk_006     1     0     0     0     0     0
